title: Minimax ATE Estimation with a Learned Vanishing Propensity and Quarter-Holder Outcomes
banked_reason: The promised Stat deliverable is an explicit matching normalization with an attaining data-only estimator and honest interval, but the core leaves that object open and supplies only a non-constant-factor lower/upper bracket.
gap_reasons: The promised Stat deliverable is an explicit matching normalization with an attaining data-only estimator and honest interval, but the core leaves that object open and supplies only a non-constant-factor lower/upper bracket.

The reproduced selected-mesh argument uses only propensity range, global tail, interval mass, the arm partition, and bin-tail; outcome Hölder and propensity Hölder are not consumed, so the lemma is stated over a gratuitously narrower class.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived fixed-order mixture lower bounds, an observable order-statistic upper bound and honest interval, and a legal growing-order lower bracket on the original class. The lower bracket retains a stretched-exponential loss against the n^(-2/5) upper scale, so it does not supply the explicit matching normalization required by the field-tier topic. A future retry needs a legal prior without the geometric order loss or a data-only estimator matching the smaller scale; tightening the existing bracket alone cannot close that gap.
tldr: For the full-population average treatment effect under quarter-Hölder outcomes and a learned propensity that may vanish, the paper proves the exact polynomial frontier but not yet the constant-factor normalization.  The observable every-second-arm-observation estimator has uniformly bounded mean squared error of order \(n^{-4/5}\), and its Chebyshev interval is finite-sample \(90\%\)-honest with length of order \(n^{-2/5}\).  A new uniform-in-order Legendre calculation strengthens the fixed-order converses to the explicit root lower envelope \(n^{-2/5}(\log n)^{-3/4}\exp\{-C\sqrt{\log n}\}\).  Determining whether that stretched-exponential loss is intrinsic, and matching it with a data-only procedure if it is, remains the exact-frontier question.
gap: Weak-overlap local moduli, clipped-AIPW normality, ordered-spacing integration, and discrete moment matching each settle a neighboring experiment, but none determines the all-procedure frontier when a quarter-Hölder propensity may vanish and must itself be learned over the stated primitive class.
fill: The paper pairs blockwise common-atom Legendre mixtures with global-tail spacing control, proves the polynomial frontier and finite-sample honesty, and reduces the exact rate to a quantitative growing-order approximation-and-testing duality.
